answer: Each agent's outputs are scored by a randomly drawn voyage of independent harnesses, so a sybil cluster gains little by vouching for itself: reputation only accrues when separate model families, data feeds, and tool stacks attest the same result. An attacker must therefore provision genuinely diverse, costly infrastructure for every fake identity, and any single colluding plume that echoes the same broken answer gets downweighted like a comet flaring briefly and fading, making each verified action cost real compute rather than a cheap clone.
